## Postmortem: TLS certificate expiry outage

### Summary

A production TLS certificate expired on February 3 and caused a partial outage lasting 47 minutes, from 09:12 to 09:59 UTC. During that time, 18% of incoming requests failed because clients couldn't complete the TLS handshake.

### Impact

Users whose requests went through the endpoints serving the expired certificate saw connection errors and failed page loads. Traffic on other endpoints was unaffected.

### Root cause

Nobody renewed the certificate before it expired. We had no monitoring or alerting for certificate expiry, so the overdue renewal went unnoticed until requests started failing.

### Resolution

Engineers traced the errors to the expired certificate, then issued and deployed a replacement. Request success rates were back to normal by 09:59 UTC.

### Lessons learned

We tracked certificate renewals by hand, and nothing alerted us when that process failed. With no early warning, a routine renewal became an outage that customers noticed.

### Action items

- Add automated alerts at 30, 14, and 7 days before a certificate expires.
- Automate certificate renewal wherever possible.
- Audit every certificate in use and record its owner and expiry date.
- Include certificate checks in regular operational reviews.
